1.title: Support, Technical Resources and Partners
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Support, Technical Resources and Partners. This is the last teaching module, and it covers task statement four point three. You will learn where to find answers on your own, how the A W S Support plans differ, how to see problems on the A W S side, and who can give you expert help. These are some of the easiest points on the exam, if you know the plan names and what each adds.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Find documentation, whitepapers, Prescriptive Guidance, the Knowledge Center and re Post. Compare the A W S Support plans: Basic, Business Support plus, Enterprise Support and Unified Operations. Say what the Support Center, the A W S Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor are for. And place A W S Professional Services, solutions architects, the A W S Partner Network and A W S Marketplace.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Plans for Trouble
1.text: Tidewater is planning for trouble. An outage on a busy night would need an engineer within minutes. The team wants guides and answers before it opens a case. Tidewater wants expert help to move its warehouse system, and software it can buy and deploy quickly. And the founder wants to know when A W S itself has a problem that affects the shop. Your job is to choose the support, resources and partners.

1.title: Self-Service Help: Documentation, Guidance and Communities
1.text: Start with free, self-service help. A W S Documentation has detailed technical guides and references for every service. Whitepapers and Guides collect technical whitepapers, decision guides and reference architecture diagrams. A W S Prescriptive Guidance offers guides for planning, and patterns with steps, architectures and code, for migration, optimization and modernization. The A W S Knowledge Center gives answers to common A W S questions, and it is hosted on A W S re Post. A W S re Post is the community question and answer site for A W S users. And A W S Trust and Safety is where you report abuse of A W S resources. The A W S Blogs and the Architecture Center add news and designs. Exam tip: search documentation, whitepapers and re Post first, and report abuse to Trust and Safety.

1.title: AWS Support Plans: Basic and Business Support+
1.text: A W S offers four support plans, and we start with the first two. Basic Support is included for every customer. It gives twenty-four-seven customer service for account and billing questions, support forums, service health checks, documentation and best practice guides, and core Trusted Advisor checks. Business Support plus adds A I-powered, contextual help, twenty-four-seven phone, web and chat with cloud support engineers, a response in under thirty minutes for a business-critical system down, the full Trusted Advisor checks, the Support A P I, and help with third-party software. It starts at twenty-nine U S dollars a month per account. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, Developer Support and Business Support end on the first of January, twenty twenty-seven, and Business Support plus replaces them, so older material uses those names. Exam tip: everyone gets Basic, and production workloads call for Business Support plus.

1.title: AWS Support Plans: Enterprise Support and Unified Operations
1.text: The top two plans add people and speed. Enterprise Support includes everything in Business Support plus, and adds a designated Technical Account Manager, called a T A M. It promises a response of up to fifteen minutes for production-critical cases, and adds A W S Security Incident Response, strategic reviews, A W S Countdown for critical events, and a five-thousand U S dollar minimum. Unified Operations pairs a T A M with Domain Specialist Engineers. Its incident managers respond within five minutes, and it adds critical workload reviews, runbooks and infrastructure event management. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, Enterprise On-Ramp ends on the first of January, twenty twenty-seven, and its customers move to Enterprise Support. Exam tip: a designated T A M means Enterprise Support or Unified Operations.

1.title: Choosing a Support Plan
1.text: Choose a plan by how critical the workload is. The figure shows the steps. Basic Support is for every customer, with self-service plus account and billing help. Business Support plus is for production workloads, with twenty-four-seven engineers and full Trusted Advisor checks. Enterprise Support is for business-critical workloads, and adds a designated T A M. Unified Operations is for mission-critical workloads, with the fastest incident response. So pick the plan by how critical the workload is, and how fast you need a human. Exam tip: the more critical the workload, the higher the plan, and a T A M starts at Enterprise Support.

1.title: Support Center, AWS Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor
1.text: Three more resources appear in this task statement. The A W S Support Center is where you open and manage support cases. Basic Support covers account, billing and service quota questions, and technical cases need a paid plan. The A W S Health Dashboard gives ongoing visibility into A W S service availability and your resources. It needs no setup, and has no additional cost. Health events also reach you through Amazon EventBridge at no extra cost, and the A W S Health A P I needs Business Support plus, Enterprise Support or Unified Operations. A W S Trusted Advisor recommends ways to cut cost, and to improve performance, security and fault tolerance, as Module five explained. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, plan details come from the Support pages. Exam tip: A W S problems that affect you mean the Health Dashboard; savings and checks mean Trusted Advisor.

1.title: Expert Help: AWS Professional Services, Solutions Architects and Partners
1.text: When you need people, three sources can help. A W S Professional Services is A W S's consulting team. It helps organizations design, build, migrate and manage A W S workloads. Think of hands-on consulting. A W S solutions architects give technical guidance on designing workloads, and the exam guide lists them as a technical assistance option. Think of design advice. And A W S Partners are independent software vendors, system integrators and consulting partners that build, migrate and run workloads. Think of help from the ecosystem. Exam tip: consulting from A W S means Professional Services; design advice means solutions architects.

1.title: AWS Partner Network and AWS Marketplace
1.text: The A W S Partner Network, the A P N, is a global community of organizations that use A W S technologies, programs, funding and tools. Partners include independent software vendors, system integrators, and consulting, training and managed-service providers. The benefits include training and certification, events and webinars, funding programs, co-selling with A W S, and A W S Marketplace listings. The exam guide also lists volume discounts. A W S Marketplace is a catalog of software, data products and professional services from independent sellers. Customers find, buy, deploy and manage them, including software as a service. It offers private offers and some free trials, as Module five noted. Exam tip: third-party software, data or services to buy on A W S means A W S Marketplace.

1.title: What the Exam Asks: Support and Resources
1.text: Here is how the exam frames this module. Self-service: documentation, whitepapers, Prescriptive Guidance, the Knowledge Center and re Post. Which plan: Basic for everyone, Business Support plus for production, and Enterprise Support or Unified Operations for a T A M. A W S problems that affect you: the A W S Health Dashboard. Savings and checks: A W S Trusted Advisor. Consulting from A W S: Professional Services; design advice: solutions architects. Partners and software: the A W S Partner Network and A W S Marketplace. And abuse: A W S Trust and Safety. Exam tip: match the need to the plan or resource: speed, a T A M, answers, consulting or software.

1.title: Design Check: Tidewater Plans for Trouble
1.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Free answers to common questions: the Knowledge Center and A W S re Post. A step-by-step migration pattern: A W S Prescriptive Guidance. Cloud engineers twenty-four-seven for the production shop: Business Support plus. A designated T A M for business-critical launches: Enterprise Support. A warning when an A W S issue affects its resources: the A W S Health Dashboard. Recommendations that cut cost: A W S Trusted Advisor. Consultants to design and migrate the warehouse system: A W S Professional Services, or an A W S Partner. Third-party software to buy and deploy: A W S Marketplace. And spam sent from an A W S address: A W S Trust and Safety. Pause the video if you want more time.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. For self-service, use documentation, whitepapers, Prescriptive Guidance, the Knowledge Center and re Post. For plans, Basic is for all, Business Support plus is for production, Enterprise Support adds a T A M, and Unified Operations is for mission-critical work. For awareness, the Health Dashboard shows A W S issues, and Trusted Advisor shows savings and checks. For experts, there are Professional Services, solutions architects and A W S Partners. And Marketplace sells third-party software, data and services.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Tidewater's production shop needs twenty-four-seven access to cloud support engineers, with a response in under thirty minutes for a business-critical outage, but it does not need a designated Technical Account Manager. Which plan fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, A W S Business Support plus. It gives twenty-four-seven access to cloud support engineers and a response in under thirty minutes for a business-critical system down. Basic Support has no technical cases, and a designated T A M starts at Enterprise Support, which the shop does not need.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Select two. Which two A W S Support plans include a designated Technical Account Manager? The five options are on the screen. The answers are C and D. Enterprise Support and Unified Operations include a designated T A M. Basic Support and Business Support plus do not, and Trusted Advisor is a tool rather than a support plan.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Tidewater wants to see when an A W S service issue affects its own resources, with no setup and at no additional cost. Which service should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, the A W S Health Dashboard. It gives all customers ongoing visibility into service availability and resource events at no extra cost. Trusted Advisor recommends improvements, Cost Explorer analyzes spending, and Artifact provides compliance reports.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Tidewater wants consultants from A W S to help design, build and migrate its warehouse system. Which option fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, A W S Professional Services. It is A W S's consulting team for designing, building, migrating and managing workloads. re Post and the Knowledge Center provide answers, and Marketplace is a catalog of third-party software, data and services.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all four answers. Question one: B. Question two: C and D. Question three: A. Question four: D. That completes Module fourteen, and the teaching content of the course. Next, Module fifteen is a quick-reference recap and a service chooser, and Module sixteen covers exam technique and a final review.
